justifications.functional_suitability: Catalog & Search Service and Catalog Management Controller address R-01 cataloging, alongside Circulation & Payments Service for circulation and Patron Web App for self-service. However, explicit mechanisms specifically differentiating physical versus digital item handling (e.g., access control or streaming/downloads) are minimal.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The dedicated Elasticsearch container, Elasticsearch Client, and Catalog Data Synchronizer decouple search from transactional loads. Read Replica and Query Caching Layer offload queries, while Envoy rate limiting protects system throughput, ensuring the 99th-percentile search response stays under 800 ms.
justifications.compatibility: The system integrates seamlessly with external systems, connecting to EU Identity Provider via OIDC/PKCE, EU Payment Gateway via HTTPS/REST, and EU-hosted Log & Telemetry Aggregator via Syslog and TLS, adhering to standard protocols like gRPC and Kafka.
justifications.usability: Patron Web App provides Search & Discovery UI and Localization & Accessibility Engine for patrons. However, Librarian / Staff and Library Administrator interact directly with the API Gateway without distinct frontend UI containers designed for their workflows.
justifications.reliability: High availability is ensured via CloudNativePG Operator with automated failover (<30s RTO) and multi-AZ deployments for Primary Database and Elasticsearch. Resilience4j in Payment Processing Component and the Transactional Outbox Publisher provide fault tolerance.
justifications.security: EU data residency constraints are enforced across EU-hosted PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, and Redis. The Edge TLS Terminator, JWT Authentication & RBAC Filter Component, column-level PII encryption, and pgaudit Extension provide robust encryption, authorization, and audit trails.
justifications.maintainability: The architecture exhibits high modularity across microservices like Catalog & Search Service and Admin & Reporting Service. Loose coupling is reinforced via gRPC, Transactional Outbox Publisher with Kafka, and clean separation of concerns within component layers.
justifications.portability: Containerized elements running standard runtimes (Spring Boot, FastAPI, React) alongside CloudNativePG Operator facilitate deployment across any EU cloud infrastructure or Kubernetes environment, with MinIO / AWS S3 EU-Central offering storage flexibility.

PERF-01.justification: Dedicated Elasticsearch cluster with multi-AZ node coordination and separate query path via Catalog & Search Service easily sustains high concurrency and meets the sub-800ms P99 latency target.
sensitivity_points: Sizing and sharding configuration of the Elasticsearch index
Envoy connection pooling and concurrency limits under peak traffic
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency between relational storage and search indexes vs lower search latency

PERF-02.justification: Asynchronous indexing via CDC isolates write transactions in PostgreSQL from search workloads in Elasticsearch, ensuring searches stay under 800 ms while propagating catalog updates well within 5 minutes.
sensitivity_points: CDC indexing pipeline lag under heavy database write traffic
tradeoffs: Near real-time visibility traded for transactional write performance and query isolation

AVAIL-01.justification: The 3-AZ Elasticsearch cluster automatically routes around failed nodes to replicas without downtime, while circulation transactions run independently against PostgreSQL, ensuring zero lost transactions and continuous operation.
sensitivity_points: Replica shard distribution across availability zones in Elasticsearch
tradeoffs: Higher infrastructure cost for multi-AZ clusters vs continuous search availability

AVAIL-02.justification: The API Gateway can route traffic away from a failed portal instance to healthy replicas with minimal downtime, while loan state resides safely in PostgreSQL, though BFF session persistence details remain partially implicit.
sensitivity_points: Session state persistence across BFF instances during unexpected node failures
tradeoffs: Server-side state isolation security vs seamless failover without shared session store

MOD-01.justification: The architecture lacks an explicit ingestion adapter or provider integration module in the Catalog & Search Service, forcing external provider integration logic into the generic Catalog Management Controller.
sensitivity_points: Coupling between core catalog domain models and external provider schemas
tradeoffs: Simpler monolithic controller vs extensible plugin architecture

MOD-02.justification: The Circulation Engine encapsulates circulation business logic directly within Spring Boot components without an externalized policy engine, rule repository, or dynamic configuration mechanism required for runtime rule modifications without code changes.
sensitivity_points: Hardcoded loan rules within compiled service components
tradeoffs: High execution speed of in-memory Java logic vs runtime policy configurability

SEC-01.justification: All persistence stores, external providers (IdP, Payment), object storage, and logging aggregators are explicitly constrained and deployed within EU boundaries by design, preventing cross-border data leakage.
sensitivity_points: Third-party services maintaining verifiable EU-only data residency guarantees
tradeoffs: Restricting vendor ecosystem to EU-compliant providers vs broader service availability

SEC-02.justification: The API Gateway enforces JWT validation and RBAC while logging to an EU telemetry aggregator. However, resource-level authorization (preventing cross-patron record access) is left implicit within the Circulation Engine rather than explicitly modeled.
sensitivity_points: Consistent enforcement of data-ownership checks at the service level
tradeoffs: Centralized perimeter RBAC verification vs granular domain-level ABAC complexity
